==English==
{{wp}}

[[Image:Eo-scale of justice.gif|thumb|right|A balance (scales)]]
[[Image:One-balanced-rock.jpg|thumb|right|A rock balanced on one corner]]

===Alternative forms===
* {{l|en|balaunce}} {{qualifier|obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{etymon|en|:inh|enm:balaunce|tree=1}}
From {{der|en|enm|balaunce}}, from {{der|en|fro|balance}}, from {{der|en|la-lat|*bilancia}}, from (accusative form of) {{der|en|la|bilanx||two-scaled}}, from {{m|la|bi-}} + {{m|la|lanx||plate, scale}}.
Displaced the word — {{m+|ang|wǣġ}} akin to Modern English: wey from {{cog|gmw-pro|*wāgu|t=scales; weight}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈbæləns/}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-balance.ogg|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|æləns|s=2}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun|~}}

# {{lb|en|uncountable}} A state in which opposing forces [[harmonise]]; [[equilibrium]].
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} Mental equilibrium; mental health; [[calmness]], a state of remaining [[clear-headed]] and [[unperturbed]].
# {{lb|en|literally|or|figuratively}} Something of equal weight used to provide equilibrium; [[counterweight]].
#: {{ux|en|These weights are used as a '''balance''' for the overhanging verandah.}}
#: {{ux|en|Blair thought he could provide a useful '''balance''' to Bush's policies.}}
# A pair of [[scales]].
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} [[awareness|Awareness]] of both viewpoints or matters; [[neutrality]]; [[rationality]]; [[objectivity]].
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} The overall result of conflicting forces, opinions etc.; the influence which ultimately "weighs" more than others.
#: {{ux|en|The '''balance''' of power finally lay with the Royalist forces.}}
#: {{ux|en|I think the '''balance''' of opinion is that we should get out while we're ahead.}}
#* {{RQ:Guardian|date=April 19, 2012
|author=Josh Halliday
|title=Free speech haven or lawless cesspool – can the internet be civilised?
|url=http://www.guardian.co.uk/technology/2012/apr/19/free-speech-haven-lawless-cesspool
|passage=The shift in the '''balance of power''' online has allowed anyone to publish to the world, from dispirited teenagers in south London to an anonymous cyber-dissident in a Middle East autocracy.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261013132321/https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2012/apr/19/free-speech-haven-lawless-cesspool|archivedate=13 October 2026}}
# {{lb|en|uncountable}} Apparent [[harmony]] in [[art]] (between differing colours, sounds, etc.).
# {{lb|en|accounting}} A [[list]] accounting for the [[debits]] on one side, and for the [[credits]] on the other.
# {{lb|en|accounting}} The [[result]] of such a [[procedure]]; the [[difference]] between [[credit]] and [[debit]] of an [[account]].
#: {{ux|en|I just need to nip to a bank and check my '''balance'''.}}
# {{lb|en|watchmaking}} A [[device]] used to [[regulate]] the [[speed]] of a watch, clock etc.
# {{lb|en|legal|business|statistics}} The [[remainder]].
#: {{ux|en|The '''balance''' of the agreement remains in effect.}}
#: {{ux|en|The invoice said he had only paid $50. The '''balance''' was $220.}}
#: {{ux|en|'''Balance''' Luzon|q=Philippine usage}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete|astrology}} [[Libra]].

====Synonyms====
* {{sense|scales}} pair of scales, set of scales, [[scales]], [[weighing machine]], [[weighbridge]] {{qualifier|for vehicles}}
* {{sense|equilibrium}} {{l|en|equilibrium}}
* {{sense|support for both viewpoints}} {{l|en|disinterest}}, {{l|en|even-handedness}}, {{l|en|fairness}}, {{l|en|impartiality}}, {{l|en|neutrality}}, {{l|en|nonpartisanship}}
* {{sense|list of credits and debits}} {{l|en|account}}

* {{antsense|support for both viewpoints}} {{l|en|bias}}, {{l|en|favor}}/[[favour]], [[partiality]], [[partisanship]], [[prejudice]], [[unfairness]]

===Verb===
[[Image:Balance.JPG|thumb|right|200px|A girl '''balancing''' on a plank of wood]]
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To bring (items) to an [[equipoise]], as the scales of a balance by adjusting the weights.
#: {{syn|en|equilibrate|q1=technical}}
## {{lb|en|intransitive|or|reflexive}} To move while remaining [[balanced]] on a narrow or precarious support (e.g., a wire, ledge or rope).
##: {{syn|en|equilibrate|q1=technical}}
##: {{ux|en|She '''balanced''' along the wire while the crowd watched in rapt attention.}}
##: {{ux|en|They must '''balance''' themselves down the fence until they reach the end.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|figurative}} To make (concepts) agree.
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2014|author=Peter Melville Logan; Olakunle George; Susan Hegeman|title=The Encyclopedia of the Novel
|passage=the Proteus Principle helps to qualify and '''balance''' the concepts of narrators and of narrative situations as previously developed in classical studies by G erard Genette and Franz Stanzel.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To hold (an object or objects) precariously; to support on a narrow base, so as to keep from falling.
#: {{ux|en|I '''balanced''' my mug of coffee on my knee.}}
#: {{ux|en|The circus performer '''balances''' a plate on the end of a baton.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To compare in relative force, importance, value, etc.; to estimate.
#* {{RQ:L'Estrange Fables of Aesop|passage='''Ballance''' the Good and Evil of Things.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|dancing}} To move toward, and then back from, reciprocally.
#: {{co|en|to '''balance''' partners}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|nautical}} To contract, as a sail, into a narrower compass.
#: {{co|en|to '''balance''' the boom mainsail}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To make the credits and debits of (an account) correspond.
#: {{co|en|to '''balance''' a set of books}}
#: {{ux|en|This final payment, or credit, '''balances''' the account.}}
#* {{RQ:Spectator|VI|549|29 November 1712|passage=I am very well satisfied that it is not in my power to '''balance''' accounts with my Maker.}}
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To be in [[equilibrium]].
# {{lb|en|intransitive}} To have matching credits and debits.
# {{lb|en|transitive|obsolete}} To [[weigh]] in a balance.
# {{lb|en|intransitive|obsolete}} To [[hesitate]] or [[fluctuate]].
